slides.title: Why Python for AI?
slides.narration:
Why Python?
It's the language of AI.
It's famous for being easy to read.
It almost looks like plain English.
The global community built incredible free tools for it.
These make working with AI much simpler.

content: Run Python code in your browser

Forget complex setups.
We will use Google Colab.
It is a free tool from Google.
You can run Python code in your browser.
No installation is needed.

slides.title: The Only Python You Need
slides.narration:
Now, for the crash course.

slides.title: Variables: Labeled Boxes
slides.narration:
Think of a variable as a labeled box.
You store information inside it.
For example, product_name = "Smart Coffee Mug".
Here, product_name is our variable.
slides.image_prompt: A visual metaphor of a labeled box with "Smart Coffee Mug" written on the box and inside, labeled "product_name".

slides.title: Strings: Pieces of Text
slides.narration:
A "string" is a piece of text.
You create one by wrapping text in quotes.
In our example, "Smart Coffee Mug" is a string.
slides.image_prompt: A simple graphic showing text enclosed in quotation marks, highlighting the concept of a string.

slides.title: Lists: Ordered Items
slides.narration:
A list holds multiple items.
They are kept in order.
Always inside square brackets [].
For example, features = ["Temperature Control", "Wireless Charging", "Digital Display"].
This is a list of features for our product.
slides.image_prompt: A visual representation of a grocery list or a bulleted list of items, with square brackets around them.

slides.title: Dictionaries: Key-Value Pairs
slides.narration:
A dictionary stores information.
It uses key-value pairs.
These go inside curly braces {}.
It's perfect for organizing related data.
For example, product_details stores product details.
It has a name, price, and stock status.
slides.image_prompt: A visual metaphor of a dictionary with words and their definitions, or a key-value data structure.

slides.title: Functions: Reusable Code
slides.narration:
A function is a reusable block of code.
It performs a specific action.
You define it once.
Then you can use it over and over.
Here is an example.
We define create_greeting.
It generates a welcome message.
Then we use it to greet Alex.
slides.image_prompt: A visual metaphor of a machine that takes an input (name) and produces an output (greeting), with the code example displayed.

slides.title: Assignment
content: Open a new Google Colab notebook.
Create variables for your favorite food.
Make a list of its ingredients.
Create a dictionary with its nutritional info.
Write a function to print a recipe step.
slides.narration:
As an assignment, please do the following.
Open a new Google Colab notebook.
Create variables for your favorite food.
Make a list of its ingredients.
Create a dictionary with its nutritional information.
Write a function to print a recipe step.
Then call that function.
